question: By a decree adopted on 28 October 20211, the Italian Ministry of Agricultural, Food and Forestry Policy established that forest trails are no longer to fall under the Italian Highway Code2 and are no longer to be used by motorised vehicles expect in a limited number of cases.

Despite this, by means of Article 4 of Law No 17 of 22 December 2023, the Umbria Region amended the regional consolidated act on forests to allow these trails to be taken by motorised vehicles unless expressly prohibited by subordinate legislative measures on signage, leaving it to a multitude of bodies to set up prohibitions and signs.

As can be seen from an Italy-wide study on these roads3, which are often located in protected sites, the legal framework is fragmented and does not provide adequate safeguards. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission consider these provisions to be consistent with the Natura 2000 targets and the EU biodiversity strategy for 2030?

Does it deem it appropriate to call on the Italian Government to adopt direct legislation and measures to ensure that forest trails are protected throughout the country with a view to upholding the environmental standards set by the EU?

Provisions defining the national minimum criteria concerning the purposes, types and technical/construction characteristics of forest and woodland-pasture roads, works related to forest management and hydraulicforestry planning. https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/eli/id/2021/12/01/21A06999/sg, Article 2(3) and (4). https://www.cai.it/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/2024-02-20-La-circolazione-dei-mezzi-a-motore-neisentieri.pdf.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.6.2024) The Commission has recently received a complaint on the matter mentioned by the Honourable Members. In this framework, it will assess whether the legislation of the Umbria region is compatible with the Habitats Directive1 or coherent with the objectives of the EU Biodiversity Strategy2 and decide on the appropriate course of action on that basis.

According to Article 6(2) of the Habitats Directive, Member States shall take appropriate steps to avoid, in the Natura 2000 sites, the deterioration of natural habitats and the habitats of species as well as disturbance of the species for which the areas have been designated, in so far as such disturbance could be significant in relation to the objectives of the nature directives.

The legislation of the Umbria region mentioned by the Honourable Members aims to regulate inter alia the use of forest roads, including in relation to motorised vehicles. The relevant regional provisions3 specify a series of restrictions, including the prohibition of motorised vehicle when indicated by relevant signs to be installed following indications by municipal administrations.

As regards Natura 2000 sites, Umbria has established special and additional provisions included in the site-specific conservation measures, that also contain restrictions for the use of motorised vehicles4.
